residue 2026-11-08-lomb-scargle-makes-two-trig-passes-per-bin-and-sample: lombScargle now computes each bin in ONE pass over the samples, in ecgdex-dsp.js, ppgdex-dsp.js and pulsedex-dsp.js. The double-angle identities give sin(2wt) and cos(2wt) from the same sin(wt) and cos(wt) the loop already needs, and the angle-difference identities return the tau-shifted sums after the loop, so four trig calls per sample become two. The algebra is exact, so only the last bits of the sums move: over 1000 bins the largest per-bin relative delta is 7.43e-11 and the total-power relative delta is 6.58e-15, against a control (the same algorithm with one beat moved by 1e-6 relative) that reads 6.62e-7. This run RE-CUT the cohort at paper scale rather than re-stamping on a claim, and the yield came back on the SAME counts: 233 tx / 239 flat, 667 / 661 skipped.
